_note: Deterministic cross-implementation test vectors. Fixed test-only seeds. The Rust client (T-RUST-1) MUST reproduce every value here. ed25519 (RFC 8032) is deterministic so signatures are pinned; RLN Groth16 proofs are NOT deterministic and are verified for equivalence elsewhere.

signalHash._note: calculateSignalHash(requestSignal(target, nonce)) — the circuit public x. keccak256(utf8(message)) as a big-endian uint, shifted right by 8 bits (drop least-significant byte), rendered decimal. message = requestSignal(target, nonce) = `rgoe:v3\n<target>\n<nonce>`. Deterministic; the Rust port MUST reproduce signalHashDecimal.

operatorAnnounce._note: Staked-announce operator vector (admission=stake proof 2). operatorSig = personal_sign(operatorAuthMessage(onion, operator)) by a FIXED test-only key. EIP-191 personal_sign over a fixed key+message is deterministic, so operatorSig is byte-pinned. verifyOperatorSig(onion, operator, operatorSig) MUST recover `operator`.

receipt._note: Signed egress success receipt (T-FEAT-13, lib/receipt.mjs). Reuses the SAME onion key as `onion`/`onionSeed`/`onionPub` above (the gateway's onion-control key signs its own receipts), so it is deterministic and cross-referable. Fixed fields {v,onion,epoch,ok}: canonicalReceiptBytes = utf8(RECEIPT_DOMAIN) || utf8(JSON with field order v,onion,epoch,ok) — epoch normalized to a decimal string. receiptOnionSig = ed25519Sign(canonicalReceiptBytes, onionSeed) (RFC 8032 deterministic, so byte-pinned). epoch=8333 is a coarse bucket, floor(1000000/120) of the announce ts, chosen only to stay cross-referable. The Rust client (T-RUST-1) MUST reproduce receiptDomain, canonicalReceiptBytesHex, and receiptOnionSig.

thresholdDirectory._note: T-FEAT-9 M-of-N threshold-signed directory. ADDITIVE: signers/signatures/threshold are OPTIONAL top-level fields EXCLUDED from canonicalDirectoryBytes exactly like the single-sig signer/signature, so the canonical bytes over this directory are byte-IDENTICAL to canonicalDirectoryBytesHex above (same {version,issued,gateways}). Each signer signs those same canonical bytes with raw ed25519 (RFC 8032 deterministic, so signatures are byte-pinned). Verify rule: >= threshold DISTINCT pinned signers with a valid sig. The Rust client (rust/rgoe-proto verify_directory) needs a threshold follow-up to consume this. Signer seeds are fixed test-only keys.

capabilities._note: T-FEAT-10 gateway capability advertisement. ADDITIVE: caps + capsSig are OPTIONAL, OMITTED from canonical bytes when absent, so the canonicalAnnounceBytes/canonicalDirectoryBytes GOLDEN vectors above are byte-UNCHANGED (an announce/directory without caps is byte-identical to before). Reuses the SAME onion key as `onion`/`onionSeed`/`onionPub`. canonicalCaps normalizes to fixed order {ports(deduped,sorted),region(coarse bucket),proto{min,max}}. capsSig = ed25519Sign(canonicalCapsBytes = utf8(capsDomain) || utf8(JSON {onion,caps}), onionSeed) — durable (no ts), onion-bound, RFC 8032 deterministic so byte-pinned. announceWithCaps.canonicalBytesHex/onionSig pin an announce that CARRIES caps (caps appended after nonce, covered by the main onion sig). directoryWithCaps pins the directory canonical bytes + bootnode signature for an entry carrying caps+capsSig. The Rust client must reproduce capsDomain, canonicalCapsBytesHex, capsSig, and both canonical-bytes hexes.

protoReasons._note: Stable public reason LABELS for wire version-negotiation rejects. Only the fixed literal prefixes are pinned — the full runtime reason strings additionally carry the offending/observed version numbers and ranges (e.g. `unsupported-version:4`, `no-mutual-version:client=1-2,gateway=5-6`), which are context-dependent and NOT pinned. badVersion/unsupportedVersion are the `label` field returned by acceptEnvelopeVersion (gateway/gateway.mjs); noMutualVersion is the reason prefix from selectProtoVersion (client/rgoe-client.mjs). The Rust client MUST emit these same literal labels/prefixes.

artifacts._note: T-HARD-8 ZK artifact-version negotiation. artifactIdOf(circuit, vkeyBytes) = `<circuit>-<sha256(bytes) hex[0:16]>` (lib/zk-artifacts.mjs; Rust rgoe_proto::artifact_id_of) — the vkey FILE bytes exactly as testdata/zk-artifacts.lock.json hashes them, so an artifact id is literally the lock hash prefix. `sample` pins the id of the utf8 bytes "hello" (sha256 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824). `reasons` are the bounded gateway/client reason LABELS (runtime strings append `:<id>` / `:client=..,gateway=..`, not pinned). `capsWithArtifacts` pins canonicalCaps (artifacts sorted, appended after proto) + canonicalCapsBytes + capsSig under the SAME onion key as `capabilities`; the pre-existing `capabilities` vectors are byte-UNCHANGED (artifacts absent => omitted).
